extracted.intended_audience: USPTO staff, patent examiners, patent quality assurance specialists, patent attorneys, and policy/research analysts studying IPR and patent examination quality
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating prosecution quality and explanatory variables associated with patents that were the subject of IPR petitions and institution decisions, using both hands-on prosecution-history review and statistical (logistic/conditional-logistic) modeling. Covers reviewer questionnaire criteria and model covariates used to predict petitioning and institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Seniority (GS-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pay grade of the allowing examiner (GS-12 and lower, GS-13, GS-14 and higher) is an explanatory variable associated with the likelihood a patent will be the subject of an IPR petition and with institution outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results show a monotonic relationship: patents allowed by GS-12-or-lower examiners have roughly 30% lower odds of being petitioned than those allowed by GS-14-or-higher examiners; GS-13 is intermediate. For institution analyses, patents allowed by GS-13 examiners are less likely to be instituted. Report odds ratios and z-statistics to assess significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity Size (Small Entity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator for whether the patent owner is a small entity; used as a key explanatory variable that strongly impacts the likelihood of IPR petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entity size is among the highest-impact variables; a model containing entity size (with foreign origin and continuation history) predicts litigation/IPR nearly as well as full models. Include in models and interpret odds ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation History
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of application continuity such as number of domestic parents and pendency from earliest parent to docketing used to capture continuation behavior and its relationship to IPR petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation history is a high-impact variable in models. Note that in propensity-score-matched models continuation history may be used to generate matches and thus not controlled for in that model specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Applications / Foreign Priority Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators for foreign-origin filings and foreign priority claims; foreign origin is predictive of petitioning/institution likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign origin variables are among the most important predictors and should be included; interpret odds ratios and consider interactions with entity size and continuation history.

rubrics_metrics.name: 371 Case (Indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator whether the application is a 371 national stage case (result of PCT national entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as an explanatory variable in logistic models; report odds ratios and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IDS Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) filed during prosecution; used as an explanatory variable for petitioning and institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings: IDS filings show a small or marginal positive effect on institution likelihood and are positively associated with petitioning in some models. Examine magnitude and significance; consider IDS content quality and volume when interpreting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Examiner Interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of substantive interviews between examiner and applicant during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR-petitioned patents have roughly 25% more interviews than control patents (propensity-score-matched sample). Include as a continuous explanatory variable and test significance; consider interviews as a marker of contested prosecution or complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency Before Examiner / Examination Pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Time (pendency) that the application spent before the examiner during examination, and more generally examination pendency measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results are model-dependent: longer examination pendency was associated with lower likelihood of IPR petition in some comparisons (forward-citation sample) but slightly longer pendency for petitioned patents in propensity-score sample. Report model-specific results and note possible inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of RCEs (Request for Continued Examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of RCE filings during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR-petitioned patents have higher numbers of RCEs. In one model each additional RCE increased odds of an IPR petition by about 18% (marginally significant in Model 4); significance varies by model. Include RCE count and report odds ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: At Least One Completed Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator whether the patent had at least one completed appeal during examination (e.g., to the BPAI/PTAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR-petitioned patents were more likely to have had at least one completed appeal (roughly double the control rate though absolute rates are small). Use as an indicator of contested prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAOM Allowance (Final After Other Matters allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that a patent was allowed after FAOM (or allowance type as captured in data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among examination variables in models; report odds ratios and assess association with petitioning/institution outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Year / Patent Issue Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorical indicators for application or issue year ranges (e.g., 1981–1995 baseline; 1996–2000; 2001–2005; 2006–2013) used to capture cohort effects and legal changes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent issue/application year can have large effects (e.g., patents issued in early 2000s were much more likely to have IPR proceedings instituted). Consider confounding with legal developments such as KSR v. Teleflex (2007) when interpreting year effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Claims Variables: Number of Independent Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of independent claims in the patent; included as a claims-structure predictor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of independent claims is a significant predictor in models (odds ratios reported). Report effect size and statistical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Claims Variables: Number of Words per Independent Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of words per independent claim (continuous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeling example: changing words per independent claim from the 25th percentile (105 words) to the 75th percentile (207 words) predicted a 23% decrease in the odds of an IPR petition. Include percentile-based effect calculations for continuous variables to communicate substantive impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Claims Variables: Functional Claim Indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator for whether the claims are functional in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in logistic models; report odds ratio and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of 3-Year Forward Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of forward citations received within three years of issue; used as a patent-value/exposure metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in institution models; report association with institution likelihood and check for collinearity with other value proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Significance and Reporting Conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of odds ratios and z-statistics to report model results, with significance denoted by ***(1%), **(5%), *(10%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report odds ratios and z-statistics with clear significance markers. Where variables are continuous, present substantive effect sizes (e.g., change from 25th to 75th percentile). Use BIC/AIC to compare model fit; note when matched variables are excluded from a matched-model specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling Approach: Conditional vs Unconditional Logistic
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of conditional logistic models with matched case-control samples (e.g., citation-matched, propensity-score-matched) for petition incidence, and unconditional logistic models for comparing instituted vs non-instituted among petitioned patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a matched control group is constructed use conditional logistic and omit matching variables used to generate the match. For the sample restricted to petitioned patents (instituted vs non-instituted) use unconditional logistic. Interpret odds ratios similarly but be aware of matched-variable omission and model-specific caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Questionnaire: Six Prosecution-History Aspects (A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questionnaire designed to gather information about six aspects of the prosecution history: A. sources of prior art relied on in the PTAB decision; B. examiner’s prior art search; C. examiner’s handling of prior art rejections; D. examiner’s handling of application continuity; E. substantive interviews between the examiner and the applicant; F. claim interpretation issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign reviewers by technical competence; a single reviewer completed all facets for each patent in the study. The questionnaire prompts reviewers to comment about reasons for examiner/PTAB differences. The design should be trialed and revised for clarity; consider blind review to reduce hindsight bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of Prior Art Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify prior art used by PTAB into whether it was previously of record (cited on IDS or provided by examiner) or newly identified by petitioner (US patent/application publications, foreign patent documents, non-patent literature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts and percentages (e.g., in study: of cases with unpatentability, 59% had prior art previously of record; 95% used third-party petitioner-supplied art). Use breakdowns to identify whether examiners had access to the same art during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for Examiner Failure to Use IDS-Cited Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Three possible causes for examiner failure to rely on prior art present in the prosecution record: (1) examiner neglects to consider applicant-supplied prior art; (2) examiner fails to understand the reference or its relevance; (3) examiner lacks sufficient time for adequate evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential remedies: remind examiners to consider IDS information per MPEP 609.01, enhance technical education and training (tech lectures, site visits, expert speakers), allocate more examiner time per case, and consider regulatory approaches to limit unduly large IDS submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Examiner’s Prior Art Search Proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer judgment about whether the examiner’s search was deficient (e.g., did not find relevant prior art later relied upon by PTAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the hands-on study reviewers judged searches deficient in over half of applicable cases, but caveats include self-selection of cases and hindsight bias. Recommendations: conduct reviewer-blind studies where reviewers perform independent searches; refine questions to separate types of search defects (database choice, search terms, operators, classification review).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS Citation Volume and 'Burying' Concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics on the number of references cited on IDS forms (average, median, and outliers) and the possibility that applicants may 'bury' material references among large numbers of documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study data: excluding an extreme outlier (2,134 references) average references cited on IDS was 128 in cases where PTAB found at least one claim unpatentable. Consider revisiting prior proposed rules limiting number/length of documents on IDS and requiring relevance explanations; assess whether voluminous IDS submissions contribute to examiner failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Process Controls and Hindsight Bias Mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural aspects of the hands-on review: single reviewer per case, reviewers assigned by technical area, trial runs and revisions to the questionnaire, and awareness of hindsight bias since reviewers knew patents had undergone IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To improve reliability: use multiple reviewers per case or blinded reviewers unaware of IPR status; ensure uniform application of questionnaire via training and clearer questions; run pilot tests and revise instrument before scaling.
